description: Trace a specific artist's creative output back through their intellectual biography to find the source texts whose structures, rhythms, and emotional registers were metabolized into fiction. Creative archaeology — reconstructing the sedimentary process by which decades of reading deposit themselves as instinct in a creative mind. Operates in two directions: archaeological (backward from art to source: 'where did the Ring learn to speak without speaking?') and alchemical (forward from source to art: 'what did the Dream of the Rood become in Tolkien's hands?'). Use when asked 'where does this come from,' 'what was the artist reading,' 'trace this back,' 'how did their reading become their art,' 'creative archaeology,' 'what's in the silt,' 'show me the metabolism,' 'how did this become that,' or any moment where a feature of a creative work invites genealogical investigation through the artist's known intellectual life.
